content.value_statement: GDPR reviews are complex when product workflows include consent, deletion, exports, and audit logs. This skill gives structured checks for privacy features and implementation reviews.
actual_capabilities: Maps product workflows to GDPR Articles 15, 16, 17, and 20.
Reviews consent capture, consent withdrawal, and audit trail requirements.
Checks deletion, anonymization, data export, and portability workflows.
Provides implementation checklist items for GDPR feature reviews.
Documents expected API endpoints, service methods, and database fields.
limitations: It is guidance for product and code review, not legal advice.
It is tailored to Empathy Ledger concepts and may need adaptation.
It does not run automated scans or verify deployed systems.
It does not replace review by qualified privacy counsel.

use_cases.title: Review a Privacy Feature
use_cases.description: Check whether a data export, deletion, or correction feature supports required GDPR rights.

use_cases.title: Audit Consent Handling
use_cases.description: Verify that consent capture, withdrawal, distribution revocation, and logging are covered before release.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Create a structured checklist for implementation evidence, audit trails, and retention behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check One GDPR Requirement
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature against GDPR Article 15, 16, 17, or 20. Identify the right involved, the required workflow, and any missing checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Consent Withdrawal
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of consent and revocation behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this consent withdrawal workflow. Check timestamps, distribution revocation, embed token handling, notifications, and audit log coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Data Deletion Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of account deletion and anonymization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this deletion design for GDPR readiness. Evaluate request tracking, 30-day processing, media removal, audit trail anonymization, and third-party notifications.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Release Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GDPR release checklist for this product change. Include data rights, consent, minimization, retention, security, audit evidence, and unresolved risks.

output_examples.input: Review a user data export feature for GDPR readiness.
output_examples.output: The review identifies Article 15 and Article 20 requirements, then checks authentication, included data categories, export format, consent records, and activity logs.

output_examples.input: Assess a story anonymization workflow after consent withdrawal.
output_examples.output: The response checks author removal, profile disassociation, media anonymization, distribution revocation, external takedown requests, and audit trail updates.

output_examples.input: Prepare a compliance checklist for account deletion.
output_examples.output: The checklist covers deletion request creation, user confirmation, processing status, media removal, profile erasure, audit anonymization, and third-party notification.

best_practices: Map every privacy feature to a specific GDPR right and user outcome.
Record consent changes and deletion actions in an auditable workflow.
Verify authentication and authorization before export, deletion, or audit access.
anti_patterns: Treating anonymization as deletion without documenting remaining data.
Allowing consent withdrawal without revoking downstream distributions.
Adding new data collection without purpose, retention, and minimization checks.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and review guidance that should be validated by qualified legal counsel.

faq.question: Which GDPR rights does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers access, rectification, erasure, portability, consent management, data minimization, retention, and audit evidence.

faq.question: Can it review code changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide review of product flows, service methods, endpoint behavior, and database fields against GDPR expectations.

faq.question: Can it verify a live system is compliant?
faq.answer: No. It does not test deployed systems, inspect production data, or replace operational compliance audits.

faq.question: Is it specific to one product?
faq.answer: The guidance references Empathy Ledger workflows, but many checklist items can be adapted to similar products.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the feature description, data fields, consent behavior, retention policy, and any relevant user journey details.
